clue.text: Of these two fighters, the heavyweight got well stoned!

definitions.text: Of these two fighters, the heavyweight got well stoned!

parts.words: Of these two fighters, the heavyweight got well stoned
parts.note: a biblical pair of combatants, the giant of whom was felled by a stone from a shepherd boy's sling; 'stoned' hints at drunkenness

explanation.surface: A tipsy prizefighter is the butt of a joke about getting well stoned after a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' wants to mean drunk or high; here it is literal: the giant warrior in the Bible was killed by a slingshot stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical giant champion of the Philistines was struck down by a stone slung by the young shepherd who fought him.

clue.text: How the Serviceman goes wrong!

parts.note: a soldier who goes wrong abandons his post without leave, the verb for running away from the forces

explanation.surface: A lament about how a soldier ends up going off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who goes absent without leave abandons his unit, the verb used for quitting military service unlawfully.

clue.text: Meaning is absolutely essential here

parts.note: the clue gives the meaning of the word wanted: something absolutely essential, indispensable

explanation.surface: Someone insists that, in this matter, having a meaning is absolutely essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable or crucial is described with this adjective, whose meaning is 'absolutely essential'.

clue.text: Just the piece of furniture for a card game?

definitions.text: Just the piece of furniture for a card game?

parts.words: Just the piece of furniture for a card game
parts.note: cards are handed out before a game, and a table made of pine planks shares the word for that handing out

explanation.surface: Someone spots a table that looks ideal for a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a British word for pine or fir timber, so a deal table is a plain pine one; the clue jokes that it suits dealing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain kitchen table of pine timber, and dealing is what a dealer does with cards before play.

clue.text: The opposite of Norfolk waterways?

parts.note: the lakes and rivers of Norfolk are named with a word meaning wide; its opposite gives a strait

explanation.surface: A question about what would contrast with the waterways of eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England; the opposite of broad is narrow, and narrows are a tight strait.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait or tight channel of water is called this, the reverse of the wide stretches famous in Norfolk.

clue.text: Birds-a large number-expressed discontent

parts.note: grouse are game birds; the word is its own plural
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Birds in a big flock make their unhappiness known.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to complain, a verb form also meaning to have voiced dissatisfaction.

clue.text: It's not dead right after making an organ

indicators.note: the letter for right comes after the word for not dead

parts.note: something not dead is alive, so live

explanation.surface: Something is declared alive just after being turned into an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The large gland in the abdomen that filters blood is a bodily organ.

clue.text: Have great loathing for mob in a tea dance

indicators.note: the letters dance about, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone detests the crowd that turned up at a tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance' looks like part of 'tea dance', a genteel afternoon social, but it signals rearranging MOB IN A TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest intensely is to loathe greatly, a formal verb for utter hatred.

clue.text: Possesses tangled gear for 16 down, so moves fast

parts.note: possesses means has

indicators.note: tangled nets are jumbled, so the letters of the gear are rearranged

parts.note: anglers at sea use nets as their gear

explanation.surface: A fisherman with knotted gear hurries off.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 down refers to the fishermen clue; their gear is NETS, and 'tangled' rearranges it to TENS after HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry is to go quickly, a verb in the same third-person form as moving fast.

clue.text: Hardened blonde is likely to stay nice!

parts.note: concrete that has hardened is set
blonde hair is fair

explanation.surface: A tough blonde will probably remain pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: A barometer marks 'set fair' for settled fine weather; 'nice' here describes the weather, not the blonde.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast of settled sunny conditions expected to continue uses this phrase.

clue.text: It's clear five get promissory note, and sob about it

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, so the pieces are rearranged together

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
an IOU is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: Plainly five people receive an IOU and weep over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges V, IOU and SOB together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain and evident to everyone is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Lions tear apart one's kin

indicators.note: the words are torn apart and their letters put back together in another order

explanation.surface: Lions rip apart a member of someone's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Family members are a person's kinsfolk, or people related to them.

clue.text: Put up someone else's money

definitions.meaning: to put something up is to lift or erect it
in poker, increasing the stake so others must add money to match; also a pay increase from an employer

explanation.surface: Someone stakes cash that belongs to another person.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift is to put up; in poker, a bet increase forces other players to match with more money.

clue.text: They write down old Jews' title

definitions.meaning: copyists who write things down by hand
in ancient Judaism, the learned teachers of the Law held this title

explanation.surface: Clerks record the ancient name of a Jewish rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyists and clerks write things down; in the Gospels, the Jewish legal teachers were known by this title.

clue.text: Apparently, one pondering a type of telescope

definitions.meaning: someone who reflects, read literally as one who ponders; 'Apparently' flags the jokey literal reading
a telescope gathering light with a curved mirror rather than a lens

explanation.surface: Someone deep in thought turns out to be a kind of telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror telescope is named for reflecting light, and one who reflects is a thinker.

clue.text: Having had them beaten, feasted riotously

indicators.note: eating riotously throws the letters into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a heavy defeat, the losers celebrated with a riotous banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description: if you have had these, you have been beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Losses in a contest are what someone has suffered when beaten.

clue.text: Catches up in their work!

parts.note: people whose job is hauling up a catch from the sea; 'catches up' pretends to mean drawing level

explanation.surface: Workers who are busy getting abreast of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches up' pretends to mean drawing level; here it is literal, pulling up the catch in nets.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers and trawlermen make their living landing hauls of fish.

clue.text: Gets less harsh German troops to go in, often

indicators.note: the troops are sent in, placed inside the word often

parts.note: the SS was a Nazi German paramilitary force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentler approach is taken whenever German soldiers march in.
explanation.definitionFit: To mellow or moderate is to make or grow gentler, a verb in the same third-person form.

clue.text: Seafood held tight, traditionally

parts.note: a small oily fish famously packed tightly in tins, giving the idiom for a crowd squeezed together

explanation.surface: A fish dish that is traditionally kept firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pilchards are canned tightly together, giving the idiom 'packed like' them for crowds.

clue.text: Schoolbooks about it? No, it's about schoolbooks, usually

definitions.text: Schoolbooks about it? No, it's about schoolbooks, usually

parts.words: Schoolbooks about it? No, it's about schoolbooks, usually
parts.note: an item that usually goes around schoolbooks, carrying them, rather than books being written about it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether schoolbooks discuss something or that thing surrounds them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' switches from 'concerning' to 'surrounding': the bag goes round the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil's shoulder bag usually holds schoolbooks, so it is literally round them.

clue.text: Changes streams in comprehensive schools? In most schools!

definitions.note: describes teachers found in most schools; a plural noun

indicators.note: a change of order, so the letters of streams are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pupils move between ability groups at comprehensives, as in most schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streams' are ability groups in British schools; comprehensives are state secondary schools. Schoolmasters are male teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Male teachers, called schoolmasters, are found working in most schools.

clue.text: Rambles around and finds something for boys to play with

definitions.text: something for boys to play with

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A walker wanders about and comes across a boy's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass balls rolled in a playground game are a traditional children's plaything.

clue.text: Content to do this? Yes

parts.note: 'content' as a verb is to please someone fully; asked whether to do this means to content, the answer is yes

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they are happy to do something, and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as an adjective, happy; it is the verb, to please fully.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone is to please them so they want nothing more.

clue.text: Wind instruments suggestive of water?

definitions.meaning: oboes, clarinets and bassoons are the woodwind family that sound through a vibrating strip
tall grasses growing by rivers and in marshes, whose presence hints at water nearby

explanation.surface: Woodwind players are asked whether their music evokes a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwinds like oboes are called after their vibrating cane strips; the same plants grow at the water's edge.

clue.text: Being rather rude? How piquant!

definitions.meaning: full of flavour, as if dressed with a tangy condiment

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how spicy a slightly cheeky remark is.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky remark is impertinent; a dish with lots of tangy dressing is also spicy.

clue.text: Was made to leave dressed in a certain way

explanation.surface: Someone was evicted while wearing a particular outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone evicted was expelled; someone smartly attired is said to be well clothed this way.

clue.text: Had brown edge going round

indicators.note: the brown edge goes round, enclosing the wanted letters within the two words

explanation.surface: A dark rim encircled something.
explanation.definitionFit: To have possessed something is to have held it as property.

clue.text: Soccer can't be played with a ball here

definitions.text: Soccer can't be played with a ball here

parts.words: Soccer can't be played with a ball here
parts.note: the area beyond the sidelines of a football pitch, where the ball is out of play

explanation.surface: A complaint about a place where football is not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' is the area outside the side lines; the phrase also means keeping in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: When the ball crosses the side line it is out of play, beyond the pitch's limits.

clue.text: Expresses oneself in a very regrettable way!

definitions.text: Expresses oneself in a very regrettable way!

parts.words: Expresses oneself in a very regrettable way
parts.note: someone who voices deep regret or grief mourns aloud

explanation.surface: Someone speaks in a manner that is badly ill-judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regrettable' seems to criticise the speaker; it means expressing regret, as in mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn or bewail is to voice sorrow and regret openly.

clue.text: Cuts shopkeepers' trade in half!

parts.note: a weekday when shops in British towns traditionally shut at lunchtime, halving the day's business

explanation.surface: Something slashes retailers' takings by fifty per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: British towns once had a weekday half-day when shops closed at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops once shut after lunch one weekday each week, so trading lasted only half a day.
